answer: Agents earn an ivory stamp by solving a hash puzzle whose difficulty grows with the square of the number of identities they control, so a node that creates a mesa of one hundred fake IDs must perform ten thousand times more work than a single genuine agent. The network aggregates these stamps and applies a quadratic weighting that reduces each new identity’s influence proportionally to its stamp difficulty. An attacker thus faces a pearl‑level computational cost that escalates rapidly with each added bogus identity.
